title: Rework focus order and screenreader announcements for dense data grid — VPAT readiness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The dense data grid (used in Dashboards > Tables and Admin > User Sessions) currently has inconsistent tab/focus order, noisy screenreader output on row selection, and some row/hover contrast combinations that fail WCAG AA for 14px body text. This ticket scopes an accessibility-first refactor: reorder interactive elements to follow DOM/focus expectations, implement concise live-region announcements for row changes, add clear keyboard affordances for range selection, and align row/background tokens with updated contrast ramp. Goal is to reach VPAT alignment for keyboard navigation and screenreader behavior for the grid component family.
background: Recent support incidents (INC-9214, INC-9340) and a customer pre-scan for a VPAT audit flagged the grid's a11y regressions. Design audits showed three core failure modes: (1) per-row action buttons interrupt natural tab flow, (2) selection state generates repeated verbose aria-labels causing screenreader churn, (3) subtle row-background color tokens drop below 4.5:1 when combined with compact text sizing. Engineering reproduced the issues with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver on Win/mac and reported complex focus management because of nested popovers and legacy cell-level interactive controls.
acceptance_criteria: Tab order follows logical reading order: row checkbox -> primary cell link -> inline actions via keyboard shortcut (not tab)
Screenreader announces concise context when moving between rows (e.g., "Row 3 of 12, selected, 4 columns") using aria-roledescription/aria-posinset/aria-setsize
Selection announcements appear in a dedicated aria-live polite region and do not repeat on focus reuse
Range selection via Shift+Arrow and Shift+Space works predictably and is documented in keyboard help tooltip
All default row/background combinations meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for body and 3:1 for large text; token changes documented in token spec
Automated a11y tests (axe + internal audit harness) added to CI and pass on supported screenreader+browser pairs
Design sign-off recorded and a VPAT pre-scan performed with remediation notes attached
tasks: Audit current implementations across DashboardTable, CompactGrid, and AdminSessionList (ENG owners: ENG-4012, ENG-4125)
Iterate token palette for row backgrounds and hover/focus accents; publish updated tokens and migration notes
Prototype focus-first DOM order and keyboard-only access to actions (avoid tabbing into inline action buttons)
Implement aria-live region and short announcement format; add debounce to avoid repeated announcements
Add examples and keyboard docs to component playground and design system site
Run VPAT pre-scan with accessibility engineering and capture findings
Ship follow-up engineering PRs and design QA checklist
design_notes_and_decisions: We will prefer DOM ordering over tabindex manipulation where possible to avoid SR inconsistencies across browsers
Inline action buttons will be accessible via an affordance key (e.g., 'a') and exposed in the keyboard help; this reduces tab stops for primary navigation
aria-roledescription on the row plus aria-posinset + aria-setsize will give succinct positional info for screenreaders without verbose cell-by-cell readout
Debounced polite aria-live (300ms) will be used for selection changes to avoid repeated announcements during multi-select operations
Contrast token changes will increase selected-row background delta and add an optional 1px focus ring token for high-density tables
risks_and_tradeoffs: Hiding inline actions from tab order reduces discoverability for keyboard-only users unless we provide clear keyboard help and affordance keys
Changing DOM ordering may require small refactors in several existing components and could impact automated E2E locators; we will coordinate with ENG to update tests
Stricter contrast tokens may slightly change visual rhythm in dense UIs — Design reviewed tradeoff and accepted the heavier focus state for a11y gains
qa_and_testing_plan: Manual passes with NVDA+Firefox, VoiceOver+Safari, and JAWS+Chrome using provided test matrix
Automated axe-run integrated in component tests with threshold assertions for live-region content length
Accessibility engineer to run keyboard-only flows for selection, sorting, inline action activation, and range selection
VPAT pre-scan: capture before/after and produce remediation notes for any remaining minor issues
